newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher, but spreads wider.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher, but spreads wider.

text.p: Morning flurries in the U.S. mortgage-backed securities market subsided toward midday Friday, leaving prices higher across the board but spreads over Treasuries modestly wider, traders said.

One institutional investor sold a large chunk of mortgages soon after inflation data pushed the market higher, one trader said. "The first thing we saw this morning was a big seller of mortgages, that widened us out a point or two," he said.
Activity wound down after the day's economic reports, traders said.
"It's been a pretty quiet day," one said.

Overall, yield spreads to Treasuries widened one or two basis points, mortgage experts said. Smaller coupons performed best, tightening to Treasuries in some instances, but current- and larger-coupon issues generally widened, they said.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent issues were 6/32 higher, at 100-29/32, yielding 109 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was up 6/32 as well, at 100-29/32 and 100-23/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury bond was up 9/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
